name: Incap Electronics US, Inc.
about:
Incap Electronics US, Inc. operates from Coal Center, Pennsylvania, as the U.S. arm of Incap Corporation, a global electronics manufacturing services (EMS) provider listed on Nasdaq Helsinki since 1997. The facility, led by Managing Director David Spehar, draws on more than 26 years of electronics manufacturing experience in the region.

The 6,500 m² plant employs 124 people and specializes in complex printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) using surface-mount and through-hole technologies. It handles medium-volume production with high SMT content and offers in-circuit testing (ICT), functional testing, validation, conformal coating, selective soldering, precision assembly, engineering support (DFM, test development), repair, rework, and lifecycle services. Additional capabilities include cable and wire harness assembly, magnetic assembly, box build, control cabinets, clean room production, and automotive-grade EMS.

Incap US serves the energy, power and charging; defence and aerospace; and e-mobility and automotive sectors. Typical applications include metering infrastructure, gas detection systems, industrial electronics and control systems, medical devices, and sensor-based technologies. The company emphasizes long-term partnerships, with some customer relationships exceeding 20 years.

The company says its differentiation lies in direct communication, fast decision-making, and a proactive approach that keeps production running smoothly. As part of Incap's global network, the U.S. site offers access to international manufacturing capacity while maintaining a local, customer-driven model focused on process control, testing, and total cost of ownership over short-term cost optimization.

name: Ind. Co. Cable TV
old_description: We offer blazing fast speeds based on Fiber or DOCSIS 3.0 Standards.
about:
Ind. Co. Cable TV, operating as Indco.net, is headquartered in Batesville, Arkansas. The company was founded in 1976 and has provided telecommunications services to communities across north-central Arkansas for more than four decades. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The company delivers cable television, fiber-to-the-home internet, DOCSIS 3.0 cable broadband, and fixed wireless internet services. Its network supports download speeds up to 1 Gbps, and all service plans include unlimited data with no caps. Indco.net also provides online bill payment and network maintenance services. Specific facility size, employee count, and subscriber volumes are not published.

Indco.net serves residential and business customers in a defined set of Arkansas communities, including Cave City, Pfeiffer, Newark, Magness, Gum Springs, Searcy, Beebe, McRae, Forrest City, Colt, Caldwell, Cushman, Judsonia, Plainview, Pleasant Plains, and Pangburn. The company positions itself as a local alternative to national providers, emphasizing a customer-focused, human-driven approach.

Indco.net states that it was built on a belief in a free and open web, which translates into unlimited data plans without forced package upgrades. The company highlights its long local presence since 1976, straightforward connection processes, and a commitment to keeping customers connected without complicated setups as key differentiators.

about:
Independent Beverage Company was founded in 1991 in Charlotte, North Carolina. The company operates from a facility near the intersection of Interstates 77 and 85 at 3936 Corporation Circle, positioning it for regional distribution.

The company specializes in cold-fill bottling and canning of soft drinks, sparkling water, and other beverages. It produces PET bottles and aluminum cans for national brands such as Cheerwine, Canada Dry, Sun Drop, 7-Up, Sunkist, A&W, Country Time, Hawaiian Punch, and Sunny D, as well as private-label retailers and contract-pack customers. Independent Beverage also markets its own CLEAR FROST™ line of sparkling waters.

Its customer base spans national beverage brands, private-label programs for retailers, and contract packaging arrangements. The facility serves the broader beverage manufacturing and contract packaging sectors, handling a range of flavors and package sizes.

Independent Beverage holds SQF Food Safety certification, underscoring its commitment to quality standards in food and beverage production.

name: Indiana Rubber & Plastic, LLC
old_description: We specialize in custom molded plastics and rubber. We offer turnkey service from idea to prototypes to volume production with custom molding and low-cost alternatives.
about:
Indiana Rubber & Plastic, LLC has operated from Indianapolis, Indiana since 1936. The company specializes in custom molded plastics and rubber, offering turnkey service from concept through prototype to volume production.

Its capabilities span prototyping via 3D printing, SLA, rapid molding, and silicone molds; rubber molding through compression, transfer, injection, and LSR/LIM processes; plastic injection molding; die cutting; extrusion of both plastics and rubber; lathe-cut rubber; machined plastics; and bonded rubber-to-metal components. The facility handles prototypes of 1–50 pieces, short runs of 1–5,000 pieces, medium runs of 5,000–25,000 pieces, and high-volume orders exceeding 25,000 pieces, with high-tonnage, large-platen presses for oversized parts. On-site tooling and proprietary low-cost Tool$aver® methods support quick-turn tooling.

The company works with a broad material portfolio including silicone, EPDM, Viton, nitrile, neoprene, fluorosilicone, and other rubber compounds, as well as engineering plastics such as PEEK, polycarbonate, nylon, ABS, and thermoplastic elastomers. It produces grommets, gaskets, seals, bumpers, diaphragms, bushings, extrusions, mounts, formed hoses, boots, and washers/spacers for customers requiring food-grade and military-specification materials.

Indiana Rubber & Plastic emphasizes three generations of experience, in-house design, chemistry, and laboratory resources, and a commitment to keeping projects “in network” by leveraging established supplier relationships. The firm highlights communication throughout the supply cycle—from inquiry through tooling, production, and shipment—as a core differentiator.

old_description: We’re excited to share an important update about Indusco Wire Rope & Fittings. Since 2011, Indusco has proudly operated under the Mazzella Companies as a standalone business. about:
Indusco Wire Rope & Fittings, based in Baltimore, Maryland, has operated as a standalone business under the Mazzella Companies since 2011. The company is privately held and family-owned.

The company supplies a broad range of lifting and rigging products including slings and assemblies, rigging hardware, wire rope, cordage, hoists, fall protection equipment, and overhead cranes. It also provides fabrication and repair services for overhead cranes and hoists, rigging training, OSHA-mandated inspections, engineered lifting devices, and metal rollforming machinery.

Its customer base spans mining, steel, oil and gas, construction, energy, shipbuilding, and vehicle and durable goods manufacturing. The merger into Mazzella's Industrial Distribution division is intended to expand resources and inventory while retaining the existing local team.

Leadership emphasizes a no-excuses, customer-first mentality and a commitment to service, safety, and reliability. The transition aims to deliver faster response times and streamlined operations without changing ownership or day-to-day contacts.

about:
Industrial Applied Electric (IAE) has operated from Bend, Oregon since 1976. The company serves Central Oregon’s industrial, fleet, and heavy-machinery sectors from a local warehouse.

IAE functions as a distributor and supplier, maintaining a fully stocked warehouse that carries starters, alternators, Deka batteries, impact sockets, rubber tracks for excavators and skid steers, Texas Refinery lubricants, Zep industrial cleaners, Milwaukee tool bundles, Hella lights, and a range of electrical components. The company offers both scheduled delivery and walk-in pickup across the Tri‑County area, aiming to minimize downtime for mechanics and fleet managers.

Customers include fleet operators, heavy‑equipment contractors, and repair shops throughout Central Oregon. Reviews on the company’s site cite M & S Equipment Services and Matrix Integrated as clients who rely on IAE for emergency parts and routine maintenance supplies.

IAE emphasizes its local inventory and knowledgeable staff as key differentiators. The company states that its warehouse enables fast, convenient deliveries without shipping delays, and that it sources only name‑brand products from manufacturers to ensure reliability.

name: Industrial Electronics By Ross
old_description: WELLER,Electronic Supply by Industrial Electronics in Milwaukee Wisconsin : Potter Brumfield, Radio Shack Stores...
about:
Industrial Electronics By Ross LLC operates from West Allis, Wisconsin, in the Milwaukee metropolitan area. The company traces its origins to 1927 when it began selling vacuum tubes and radio parts. It is certified as a woman-owned small business and holds CAGE code 5A8Z1.

The firm acts as a franchised distributor for 116 electronic manufacturers, offering access to over one million distinct items ranging from electron tubes to modern integrated circuits. Its product portfolio includes chemicals such as acrylic coatings, contact cleaners, and flux removers; heat-dissipative products like cold plates and extrusions; and pre-assembled component kits for Raspberry Pi and Arduino platforms. The company also provides just-in-time (JIT) supply services and operates an employee-managed structure in which 99 percent of sales decisions are made at the first level.

Customers serve the industrial electronics marketplace, including original equipment manufacturers, maintenance and repair operations, and educational or hobbyist buyers seeking prototyping kits. The distributor’s line card features brands such as Potter & Brumfield, Weller, Molex, and Panasonic, covering relays, connectors, soldering tools, and passive components.

The business emphasizes its long history, employee-managed decision-making, and JIT capability as key differentiators. Its woman-owned status and federal cage code support government and prime-contractor procurement requirements.

name: Industrial Fabrics, Inc.
old_description: Since 1981, Industrial Fabrics has proudly served many diverse clients in the construction, industrial and residential industries along the Gulf Coast and around the world.
about:
Industrial Fabrics, Inc. (IFI) was founded in 1981 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, as a manufacturer and distributor of geosynthetic solutions for infrastructure projects. The company pioneered the geosynthetic industry along the Gulf Coast and has since expanded its reach worldwide.

IFI produces a portfolio of branded geosynthetic systems including RockGuard pipeline protection mesh, GrassGuard turf reinforcement, EnviroTubes dewatering and containment tubes, GreenSolutions erosion control blankets, and BaseLok soil stabilization geogrids and GeoCell systems. Operating from a new $8 million production facility, the company offers full-service manufacturing, custom fabrication, design assistance, material logistics, and on-site technical support. To date, IFI has supported over 5,000 projects across more than 20 states and maintains over 10 strategic product brands.

The company serves a broad range of sectors: commercial and industrial development, roadways and highways, railways and mass transit, energy and utility infrastructure (including wind turbine pads and solar farm access roads), residential development, coastal and marine waterways, ports and intermodal facilities, airports, data centers, electrical distribution, petrochemical and chemical plants, oil and gas facilities, government and public works, waste management and containment, military and defense applications, mining, and temporary housing. Customers include engineers, contractors, and government agencies worldwide.

IFI differentiates itself through its on-staff registered engineers who provide design assistance, material selection, and installation guidance; ISO-certified manufacturing with rigorous testing; continuing education (CEU) seminars for engineers and contractors; and a mission to deliver engineered geosynthetic solutions that strengthen, protect, and preserve global infrastructure through innovation, integrity, and sustainability.

name: Industrial Finishes
old_description: Industrial Finishes is proud to be Featuring 3M products Since 1958
about:
Industrial Finishes, founded in 1958, operates a branch in Reno, Nevada The Reno location originated from the acquisition of Barrett Paints and Re-Neva Paint, which Industrial Finishes purchased and refreshed in 2012 to include one of the area's few educational centers for finishing training. The company is a distributor of 3M products and other finishing supplies, though founder names and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The Reno facility distributes a broad line of paint finishes, industrial coatings, paint supplies, surface preparation products, hand power tools, equipment, abrasives, safety products, clips and fasteners. It also houses an educational center with capacity for 50 people, used for I-CAR certification classes, association meetings, and product demonstrations. The team provides business support and develops custom finishing systems for applications that "roll, float, or fly." Collective staff experience exceeds 100 years.

The branch serves customers within a 150-mile radius, covering Reno, Sparks, Carson City, South Lake Tahoe, and parts of California. Key sectors include automotive refinish, construction, aerospace, military, RV and specialty vehicles, and industrial panel finishing. A noted customer is Drone America, a major drone supplier to the U.S. government, for whom the team develops specialized coating solutions.

Industrial Finishes emphasizes that the sale is only the beginning of their duty, aiming to re-win business daily through timely delivery and technical support. The educational center and focus on custom system development differentiate the distributor in a market where hands-on training and application expertise are scarce.

name: Industrial Metal Enterprises, LLC
old_description: Let us provide you with your auger needs and screw flights using our Super Tyro AST machine utilizing Tru-Helix flight forming technology.
about:
Industrial Metal Enterprises, LLC operates from Blackfoot, Idaho, where it was founded in 1993. The company has served industrial, commercial, and residential clients across eastern Idaho for over three decades.

The shop runs a Haas TM-2P CNC mill with a 10,000 RPM spindle, a water jet cutter, and a CNC plasma table for custom metal fabrication, including structural steel, sheet metal, and ornamental work. A Super Tyro AST machine equipped with Tru-Helix flight‑forming technology produces sectional screw flights and complete augers — the only such system in the western United States, according to the company. In‑house capabilities cover design (with 3D drawings submitted for approval), welding, pipe fitting, boiler and steam fitting, mobile welding, and on‑site repairs. Materials processed include stainless steel, carbon steel, aluminum, and specialty alloys, plus slip‑resistant surfaces such as SlipNOT and All‑Grip.

Customers span food‑processing plants requiring sanitary conveyors and decks, as well as general industrial, commercial, and residential projects needing platforms, handrails, stairs, safety gates, caged ladders, roof flashings, and custom augers.

The firm emphasizes on‑time delivery, competitive pricing, and a start‑to‑finish approach that handles planning, design, fabrication, and installation under one roof.
